Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run set for spring 2027. It will be her first full tour of the region since she stepped away from performing in 2025. Since returning, she has chosen one-off shows and festival appearances instead of immediately rebuilding the schedule she cancelled. The new dates change that: for the first time since the break, several weeks of shows are back on her calendar.

The break began after she collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York and then cancelled her remaining performances for the foreseeable future. In the message that followed, she said she needed time to work on herself and asked listeners to give her "a second chance" when she was ready to return. She did not attach a comeback date to that promise. When she eventually came back, it was through individual appearances rather than a replacement for the North American tour built around *I'm Only F**king Myself*.

The Grammys gave that return its biggest stage. "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance, and she performed the song during the ceremony. Headline shows in Britain and festival appearances followed, including a return to All Things Go. By the time the 2027 dates were announced, she had already spent months onstage again. What had been missing was the commitment to weeks of headline shows in the same region.

[apple:song:6768357139:6768357142]

"From Down Here" arrived during that stretch and gave her new material written after the break. She has said the idea hit the day after the Grammys and led her into the studio with James Blake. The song looks back at the pull of an old high while valuing a more grounded life, and the music is calmer than much of *I'm Only F**king Myself* without smoothing out her blunt writing. It gives the next shows a song that belongs to this period of her life rather than only material from the album cycle that was interrupted.

The tour name, "Everything Begins," flips the wording of her "Everything Ends" tattoo. After months of choosing individual appearances, she is willing to put several weeks of shows on the calendar again. The phrase now describes something concrete rather than aspirational. The return is no longer being measured one night at a time. It now has a beginning, a middle and an end already booked.
